title: Derived open-closed conservativity for arbitrary coefficients
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian coefficient category, and let $j:U\to X$, $i:Z\to X$ be complementary open and closed immersions of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. On the ordinary unbounded derived categories of small etale $\mathcal A$-valued sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-etale-site], the pair $(D(j^*),D(i^*))$ jointly reflects isomorphisms.

proof.text: At the sheaf level a sheaf killed by j^* is i_*G: base change i.Etale is cover-dense and locally full and faithful; its induced-topology sheaf equivalence applies because adjoining the etale objects over U turns every induced cover into an etale cover, and the given sheaf vanishes on those objects. The source Supported.lean proves this for arbitrary Grothendieck abelian coefficients.
If i^* also kills the sheaf, the invertible counit i^*i_*G to G makes G zero. Exact inverse images therefore detect zero kernels and cokernels, giving joint reflection of isomorphisms on sheaves.

Exact inverse images commute with all homology objects. If both derived restrictions invert a map, they invert each homology map. Sheaf-level joint conservativity makes every homology map invertible, so the derived map is invertible.
